links.outcome: Hallucination rate of evidence-grounded retrieval system versus ungrounded baseline on 100 clinical-style queries
links.effect: No hallucinated answer observed with grounding (100% database grounding) versus a 41.0% no-hallucination rate for the ungrounded baseline; internal validation only.
links.quote: No hallucinated answer was observed under the study’s operational definition, compared with a 41.0% no-hallucination rate for the ungrounded baseline.

unlisted_practices: Abstention/rejection rule that suppresses answers when retrieval support falls below a prespecified threshold
Entity-aware retrieval (gene, variant, cancer-type matching) over a curated multi-source oncology knowledge base

screen.reason: The study evaluates a RAG framework incorporating evidence retrieval and confidence-based rejection rules against an ungrounded baseline, specifically measuring hallucination reduction and grounding.
